clue.text: How Edward is entitled to consult about oil company boss being sacked

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, here the verb for consulting wrapped round the firm

parts.note: to confer is to consult

indicators.note: the boss is the head, so losing the boss means the first letter of the firm's name is dropped

parts.note: Esso is a well-known oil company brand

explanation.surface: An oil company chief has been fired, and someone confers about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss being sacked' drops the firm's first letter; 'about' puts what is left inside the verb, between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward the Confessor bore this title, so it is how that Edward is styled.

clue.text: Bravery of old university rector put in prison

indicators.note: put in means these letters are placed inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a prison

explanation.surface: An old college head is jailed and shows his mettle.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and bravery are synonyms for facing danger without fear.

clue.text: Here's me losing nothing in change when providing coinage

indicators.note: in change means these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A person loses no money in their change when paying with coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coinage' and 'change' both pretend to be money; coinage here means inventing words.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a newly invented word or expression.

clue.text: A suitable moment to return by short cut — they're giving out

indicators.note: to return means the word for a suitable moment is read backwards

parts.note: a time is a suitable moment, as in 'now is the time'

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is trimmed off

parts.note: terse means short, brief

explanation.surface: Someone waits for the right moment to head back by a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short cut' is not a quicker route: TERSE (short) is cut to TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that emit, such as radiation sources, are giving out signals or energy.

clue.text: Reason for hanging around court is pure quality

indicators.note: hanging around means the reason word surrounds the court letters

parts.note: sanity is reason, sound mind

explanation.surface: A lawyer argues the reason for loitering near the court was entirely innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiness or sacredness is a quality of purity.

clue.text: Horseman arrests amateur looter

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the horseman's word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a rider is a horseman

explanation.surface: A mounted policeman catches a part-time thief.
explanation.definitionFit: One who raids in order to plunder is a looter.

clue.text: Two different men on the board have coffee say

parts.words: Two different men on the board
parts.note: on a chessboard B is a bishop and R a rook, two different pieces
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Two company directors sit down to a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men on the board' suggests company directors; here they are chessmen, with B for bishop and R for rook.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is an example of the colour, hence 'say'.

clue.text: How far across (ignoring depth)? A lungful's required

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter is left out

parts.note: breadth is how far across something is

explanation.surface: Measuring the width of a pool, depth aside, takes a deep breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Air drawn into the lungs once fills them, a single inhalation.

clue.text: Very heavy gongs with extra echo

parts.note: gongs is slang for medals and honours, such as OBEs
E is Echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Huge gongs with an extra ringing echo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gongs' is British slang for medals or honours; the OBE is the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Being severely overweight means being very fat and heavy.

clue.text: Close old-fashioned strap in nocturnal attire

parts.note: nigh is an old-fashioned word for close or near
a tie is a strap or fastening

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned strap fastened on bedtime clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn in bed at night is nightwear.

clue.text: Looking like an ideal place to deal out pain

indicators.note: to deal cards is to shuffle them out, so the letters of these words are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a perfect place where no pain is dealt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is the imagined perfect society, so something resembling it is idealistic in that way.

clue.text: I see diver returning to a shipping hazard

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like the word see

indicators.note: returning means the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: the grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: Someone spots a diver coming back toward a danger to ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' is not a swimmer but a diving water bird; 'returning' turns its name round.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating ice masses have long endangered vessels, the Titanic most famously.

clue.text: Take trouble with exercises

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
PT is physical training, exercises

explanation.surface: Someone goes to some effort over their workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a child or an idea as one's own is to adopt it.

clue.text: Time's right to take what cannibals do for therapy

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, the 's joining it to what follows

indicators.note: to take means the abbreviation for right holds the next phrase inside it

parts.note: cannibals eat men

explanation.surface: A darkly comic idea that eating people might be a kind of cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical or psychological care given to a patient is their course of therapy.

clue.text: Ukraine at last! How fast Russian fighters move to settle in a new country

definitions.text: move to settle in a new country

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the country name

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
rate is speed, how fast something goes

explanation.surface: A war report on how quickly Russian jets reach Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer puts the jets before their speed, a speed of jets, so the pieces join in the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one's homeland to live permanently abroad is exactly to resettle in another country.

clue.text: Pick out some minerals here — sounds like a great deal

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for a great deal is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: loads, or a load, is a great deal

explanation.surface: A miner's tip: dig here, as there's plenty to be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' is the miner's tool: a vein of ore is where you pick out minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein of metal ore in rock is the place from which minerals are mined.

clue.text: Barring twisted racists is in order

indicators.note: is in means the jumbled letters sit inside the order letters

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are distorted into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A statement that excluding warped bigots is quite proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' looks like 'proper'; it is the Order of Merit, OM, holding STRACIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusion from society or a group is a form of barring someone.

clue.text: Sierra on high above most of one great lake or another

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet
up means on high

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A mountain range towers above one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' looks like mountains but is the radio code word for S; the definition 'another' means a further Great Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Superior is a further one of the North American Great Lakes beside Erie.

clue.text: Something missing in a boy's slanders

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the boy's name

parts.note: Ben's is a boy's, Ben being a boy's name
a lack is something missing

explanation.surface: A boy's spiteful slanders reveal some lack in him.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacken someone's name is to defame or slander them.

clue.text: A spell let out rebounds

indicators.note: something that rebounds comes back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to let out

explanation.surface: A magic spell is released and bounces back on its caster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks magical but means a period, as in a spell of weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of something is a period or stretch of it.

clue.text: Walking out of Spain in traffic

indicators.note: out of means the letter is taken away

parts.note: treading is walking
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Walking out of Spain amid busy traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' is a verb or noun for commerce, not cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in goods means dealing or commerce, buying and selling.

clue.text: A period of all-out strike?

parts.note: all-out means total, full
to strike is to stop work

explanation.surface: A spell of total industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the dot ending a sentence is called a period.

clue.text: Maybe 1Ac, 6Ac, 18Ac or 29 and 14, 28, 1Dn, 16 or 21 — one of them has a lease

parts.note: pa is an informal word for a father, one of the pair
someone who rents holds a lease

explanation.surface: A puzzle-wide roll call of famous figures, one of whom is a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: Each cross-referenced answer follows Father or Mother: Father Confessor, Father Brown, Father Time, Father Christmas; Mother Lode, Mother Goose, Mother Courage, Mother Superior, Mother Tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathers and mothers are mum and dad, the theme's two titles.

clue.text: Polish maybe kept in toilet on guest-nights

indicators.note: kept in means the letters are held within these words

explanation.surface: On guest nights polish is kept in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like cleaning stuff but is the language of Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is an example of a language, a mother's speech.

clue.text: The French put in this for cooking — it might make us allergic

definitions.text: The French put in this for cooking — it might make us allergic

indicators.note: cooking means mixing up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: French cooks put a pungent bulb in their food, though it may disagree with some of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Add LE to the answer and cook the letters, and you get ALLERGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The pungent bulb is famously a staple of French cookery and some people react to it.

clue.text: A long time to hold a job mostly — it provides security

indicators.note: to hold means the long stretch of time wraps round the job

parts.note: an age is a long time

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a job

explanation.surface: Keeping a job for ages brings security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A long time' is read as the phrase 'an age', which holds the shortened job.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring place for ships keeps them secure, and figuratively any source of stability.

clue.text: A big fiddle as the big cheese snorts lines

indicators.note: to snort lines is to take them in, so the lines go inside

parts.note: the CEO, chief executive officer, is the big cheese
L is the abbreviation for line, LL for lines

explanation.surface: A fraudulent boss snorts lines of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big fiddle' looks like fraud; it is a large stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument is a larger relative of the violin, colloquially called a fiddle.

clue.text: It'd be cleaner if I wasn't sat in it

indicators.note: the clue says the thing would be the cleaner if the letter were not sitting in it, so the letter is placed within the cleaner's word

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner, a British term

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in a seat admits it would be cleaner without them.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is a British word for a cleaning lady; the clue says the answer, minus the I sat inside it, would be that cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to the seat one sits in, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: I will say almost everything is not allowed

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all is everything

explanation.surface: Someone insists on having their say on everything that is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives EG, the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something against the law is forbidden, prohibited by rules.

clue.text: Maybe Spaniard comes from cold region of Russia setting off south

indicators.note: setting off means sending away, so the letter is removed

parts.words: comes from cold region of Russia
parts.note: a Siberian comes from Siberia, the cold region of Russia

explanation.surface: A Spaniard turns out to hail from Siberia but heads south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting off south' reads like travel; it removes S from the front of SIBERIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spaniard is an example of someone from the peninsula shared by Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Go to sea when short of time and with no adult? Silly person!

indicators.note: with no means the next letter is missing too
short of means lacking, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to sea in a hurry and alone, a foolish plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T and A from GO TO SEA and GOOSE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a goose is a mild way of saying they are a fool or silly.

clue.text: A time for celebrating its charms perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be put another way, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A festive season praised for its charms.
explanation.definitionFit: The December festival is a season of feasting and festivity.
